claim: Controls how this shot arrives on screen — snapped in hard on a cut, bled up out of black, or thrown in on a whip pan — and it lives on the shot that owns the change rather than on some seam between shots. A director reaches for it to set how much ceremony an entrance gets: a smash into a face and a slow dissolve into a memory are the same field, one word apart.
not_visual: A transition is an event between two shots, and a still has no outgoing shot to arrive from — the variable's entire content is what happens across the boundary. The options with a visible mid-transition frame degrade into unrelated lessons: fade_black renders as a dim scene, fade_white and flash as a blown-out one, dissolve as a double exposure, whip_pan as motion blur, so the panel would teach exposure and blur rather than arrival. Worse, cut, smash and match_cut have no single-frame signature whatsoever, so three panels would come back byte-identical to the base subject and the grid would read as a broken render rather than an honest zero.
